locations.rationale: Property access `this.title` inside Greeter.greet resolves to the instance property created by the declaration `this.title = title;` in the constructor of the same class.
Constructor parameter declaration `title` introduces a distinct local binding; it is not the instance property.
Right-hand-side `title` in `this.title = title;` resolves to the constructor parameter binding, not the instance property.

records.rationale: The declaration is the instance property `title` assigned in the Greeter constructor (`this.title = title;`). The only exact-name token that semantically resolves to this property outside the declaration token is the `this.title` access in Greeter.greet (line 8, chars 19-24). The constructor parameter `title` (line 3) and the RHS `title` (line 4) resolve to the parameter binding and are excluded. No other file contains a `title` token: app.js uses DEFAULT_TITLE (different identifier, substring only) and the CommonJS files reference only `accepts`. No import/export binding tokens exist for the property, so no optional binding locations apply under bindings_optional. definitionUsage is the sole required location.
